First aid was provided by thoroughly irrigating the wounds with normal saline solution, followed by the application of povidone-iodine (Betadine) and sterile gauze dressings to help prevent infection.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team conducted a primary assessment of both patients, including their levels of consciousness, presence of active bleeding, and any apparent injuries or deformities. Both patients were found conscious, alert, and oriented. Patient #1 sustained a bump on the forehead and complained of dizziness following the incident. Patient #2 was assessed with a suspected fracture of the right shoulder.
First aid was provided to both patients. Patient #1 was carefully secured onto a stretcher using appropriate straps to minimize unnecessary movement during transport. Vital signs and neurological status, including the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and pupillary response, were monitored due to the forehead injury and reported dizziness. Patient #2's right upper extremity was carefully supported and immobilized using an appropriate splint to minimize movement and prevent further injury.
The patients were immediately transported to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, the patients were properly endorsed to the medical staff on duty.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || While conducting a house-to-house survey at Purok Anunang, Barangay Dalangin, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, Shift B personnel received a report of a medical emergency at Palomoc National High School and proceeded to the location. 
Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team found the patient seated inside the school clinic, conscious and initially alert but experiencing hyperventilation and difficulty breathing. Attending teachers reported that the patient had experienced a previous loss of consciousness and that a paper bag had been placed over the patient's mouth. The EMS team conducted an initial assessment, checked the patient's airway, breathing, and circulation, and monitored vital signs and level of consciousness. The patient was assisted into a comfortable seated position, reassured, and encouraged to breathe slowly while being continuously monitored.
The patient was carefully transferred onto a stretcher and secured for transport to the BFP ambulance. The responding EMS personnel provided the necessary support and continuously monitored the patient’s level of consciousness and overall condition during the transfer.
The patient was promptly transported via BFP ambulance to the Titay Rural Health Unit (RHU) for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at the Titay RHU, the patient was safely transferred and formally endorsed to the physician on duty, together with the pertinent assessment findings, for further medical evaluation and management.

EARTHQUAKE INFORMATION | PHIVOLCS ADVISORY

A Magnitude 2.3 earthquake was recorded by PHIVOLCS today, 26 June 2026, at 7:09 PM, with its epicenter located 18 km North 22° West of Sarangani Island, Davao Occidental, at a depth of 81 km.

At this magnitude, no damage and aftershocks are expected.

Although this was a minor earthquake, it serves as a reminder that our municipality should always be prepared for any emergency.

🔹 Safety Reminders:
✅ Stay calm and avoid spreading unverified information.
✅ Familiarize yourself with safe evacuation areas and emergency exits.
✅ Prepare and maintain your emergency go bag.
✅ During strong earthquakes, remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
✅ Follow only official updates from PHIVOLCS and LDRRMO-Titay.

Let us remain vigilant and always practice disaster preparedness. Being prepared today can save lives tomorrow.
